subject: Congestion gating playbook & reserved GPU isolation — proposal for NimbleWave

From: Ava Collins <ava.collins@nimblewave.ai>

Cc: procure@nimblewave.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: playbook for congestion gating + reserved GPU isolation

Hi Rishi,

Quick note from NimbleWave's SRE and procurement teams — we've started hitting tail-latency spikes during peak inference loads on our Reserved GPUs (mostly during daily batch windows and occasional traffic bursts). Our legal/procurement folks are asking for a clear operational playbook that explains how Redwood will isolate our reserved capacity, what gating/queueing behaviors we can expect, and what remediation steps you will take if we observe sustained throughput degradation.

Specifically we need:
- A short runbook describing congestion gating rules (priority lanes, preemption thresholds)
- Expected impact on concurrent requests when the pool is 90%+, 95%+, 99% utilized
- How burst crediting or headroom works and whether we can buy additional short-term headroom
- SLAs/credits related to throughput shortfalls

Could you share a proposed playbook and any contract addenda we should send to our procurement team? We're targeting a renewal conversation in early August and want this clarified before then.

Thanks,
Ava Collins
Director of Platform Reliability
NimbleWave

Subject: RE: Request: playbook for congestion gating + reserved GPU isolation

Thanks Ava — appreciate the clear list. Looping in Ben (solutions) and Laura (account lead) so we can provide a short playbook and the contractual wording.

High-level answer up front: Redwood can provide a formal "congestion gating" playbook that documents priority lanes, preemption policy, and short-term headroom purchase options, plus an addendum that maps those behaviors to throughput credits and remediation SLAs. We have a draft ready that covers:
- Queueing behavior by priority lane (default, reserved, emergency)
- Trigger thresholds and deterministic preemption for best-effort vs reserved lanes
- Short-term headroom: 1–48 hour bursts purchasable as a credit bucket (configurable)
- Observable signals and runbook steps (alerts, kill/fallback to smaller model, autoscale suggestions)

Ben — can you attach the technical matrix for reserved GPU isolation and fill in the utilization impact numbers? Laura — procurement wording and billing language (credits) needed. I'll assemble and send the draft by EOD.

Rishi
VP, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: playbook for congestion gating + reserved GPU isolation

Ava — attaching the technical isolation matrix and a short appendix that shows the measured impact on tail P95/P99 when isolation modes are applied. Highlights:

- When pool utilization crosses 90%: reserved lanes are maintained; best-effort requests may see queueing with median latency increase ~12–18% for 512-token runs.
- At 95%+: preemption for best-effort begins; we cap inflight requests per tenant based on negotiated concurrency (we enforce tokens-in-flight). This prevents phantom queuing and keeps P99 from spiking beyond the contracted cap in most cases.
- At sustained 99%+: we trigger emergency backpressure and will automatically (a) surface a headroom purchase option to the Console and (b) fall back low-priority workloads to smaller quantized variants.

Operational controls available to NimbleWave (configurable):
- Priority lanes: reserved (untouchable unless you opt-in), standard, overflow
- Soft headroom: automated short bursts up to X tokens/min from a credit bucket (configurable, billable)
- Hard preemption: kill best-effort requests beyond concurrency threshold

Notes on billing/credits: the addendum we propose ties throughput shortfalls >10% for a 6-hour window to a pro-rated credit (formula included in attached spreadsheet). That language is intentionally narrow to keep operational flexibility.

Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: reserved_gpu_isolation_matrix.xlsx

Subject: RE: Request: playbook for congestion gating + reserved GPU isolation

Ava — thanks for the patience; we reviewed the attachments and drafted a short contract addendum to include with your renewal paperwork. High-level:

1) Service behavior: we commit to the priority lane semantics and the preemption thresholds outlined in Ben's matrix.
2) Credits: if measured throughput to NimbleWave's reserved pool falls below 90% of the contracted baseline for any contiguous 6-hour window (and the drop is caused by Redwood infrastructure or routing decisions), NimbleWave will be eligible for pro-rated usage credits as described in the attached Doc (we've kept the formula conservative).
3) Short-term headroom: NimbleWave can opt into a rolling headroom credit bucket (configurable via Console) for up to 48 hours at negotiated rate.
4) Escalation/playbook: we will notify designated SRE contacts, open an incident, and provide a remediation timeline (initial triage in 30 minutes, mitigation plan within 2 hours).

Please confirm if the thresholds above are acceptable or if you want a harder SLA (we can discuss increasing credit levels but that affects pricing). If acceptable, we can circulate a DocuSign addendum for signature and include the playbook as an appendix to the Reserved Capacity Exhibit.

Laura Bennett
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
